t.E962.agn: In 2023 IARC classified aspartame in Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic to humans); in the same year JECFA did not change the daily limit of 40 mg/kg.
t.E962.body: The aspartame it contains breaks down in the digestive tract into phenylalanine, aspartic acid and methanol; for this reason, the warning “contains a source of phenylalanine” is mandatory on the label.
t.E962.eff.0.t: It is a source of phenylalanine; it may raise the phenylalanine level in the blood. In the EU the warning “contains a source of phenylalanine” is mandatory on the label
t.E962.eff.1.t: In 2023 IARC placed the aspartame it contains in Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic to humans); in the same year JECFA did not change the daily limit
t.E962.eval: Contains aspartame: in 2023 IARC classified aspartame as Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic). For people with phenylketonuria, the warning “contains a source of phenylalanine” is mandatory on the label.
t.E962.prod: A sweetener produced by chemical synthesis.
t.E962.summary: The combined salt of aspartame and acesulfame K. Used in diet drinks and chewing gum.
t.E962.what: The combined salt of aspartame and acesulfame K; it gives sweetness in very small amounts.
t.agency.EU_phenylalanine_label: The warning “contains a source of phenylalanine” is mandatory on the label (1169/2011 Annex III).
t.flag.phenylalanine.0: It is a source of phenylalanine; the label carries the warning “contains a source of phenylalanine”.
